title: Retain heavy transition modes and pay their Bayes excess
statement: Use a common soft effect0<=F<=M on K=p sigma-q tau. Heavy near-tie modes are retained: alpha_F+beta_F=e+Tr[(M-F)K]<=e+r kappa*. Learned logical-isotropic error<=2sqrt(5Delta)+0.495nu p; this is not an entropy-to-overlap claim.

requires: Fixed finite-dimensional stationary memoryless source; data/reference and every fresh program independent conditional on ONE fixed source. Known accessible output-register type, trusted qutrit/ancilla gates, coherent whole-register SWAPs and quantum memory. No purification, inverse oracle, hidden flag, unknown eigenbasis or reusable decoder is supplied. Unknown tensor isometry V:C3 tensor F->B and LOGICAL-ISOTROPIC reset. H_j=4T_j-8omega; matching positive Bell sectors depend on K=p sigma-q tau. Soft transition modes may carry LARGE success mass; charge Bayes excess<=r kappa*, not discarded-success mass.

assumptions: Logical-isotropic reset is essential. No arbitrary overlapping mixed-reset or entropy-to-code-overlap theorem follows. The Helstrom measurement needs discrimination data; the learned theorem acquires an effect separately. Square-root deficit error is sharp even at fixed p=q=1/2 and rank-two flags by a separable bad-block arbitrary-decoder witness. Unrestricted WH3 entropy/VALUE and general mixed-success recovery remain OPEN. These conditional model theorems do not verify source promises, stationarity, Delta, hardware, novelty, advantage, unassisted capacity or finite-block coding.

Gate width/storage depend on output dimension even when sample count does not. Each datum consumes a new bank; no free batching or demonstrated practical advantage. kappa*=nu p0/(16r),xi=nu/100,M>=1152/kappa*,L=ceil log16[1000/(p0xi)],R=ceil log2(1/eta),S=9LR pi(M-1); n_train<=2*10^10 S²/xi+36LRm plus datum.
